verdicts.rationale: The stated reasoning is literally the trace of a rule engine: every decision cites a hand-percentile, a position-based open frequency, and an RNG roll ("roll 0.88 said open"), with identical phrasing templates across players. Table-read tags are appended word-for-word to multiple players simultaneously and sometimes in nonsensical contexts (hand 27's "raiser re-raises light" on a limped pot), and several players share the exact same equity-vs-price sentence frame. Personas are differentiated by design (calling station, loose-aggro, nit) but there is zero mood, memory, or reaction to big hands — clearly scripted algorithms.

Each player is a fixed catchphrase generator: Mikko's "Nearly limped X out of boredom. Nah.", Dunn's "Almost limped X again. Letting it go.", and Vera's "Been waiting a while for something like X" recur verbatim with only the hand slot swapped, and read-tags like "The raiser re-raises light — seen it plenty" get appended mechanically to every action in a hand regardless of relevance. There are visible template bugs ("Checking. something thin doesn't want a big pot.", "a big hand is strong — calling") and unfilled-slot lines, plus algorithmic tells like exact equity-vs-price percentages and nonsense sizings (Mikko "raises to 4" over a 110 bet). Personas are differentiated, but by parameter, not personality — no mood drift, no reaction to the massive pots won or lost, no memory across hands beyond a canned read string.

The reasoning lines are transparently fill-in-the-slot templates: each player has a fixed handful of phrases that recur verbatim regardless of context ("Come along if you dare", "Been waiting a while for something like X", "X almost talked me into a limp"), and slot-insertion produces grammar artifacts no human would type, like "Checking. not much doesn't want a big pot" and "something thin. Free card sounds good." Calls are justified with suspiciously precise equity percentages ("About 90 percent with the price at 35"), and the table-read tag "The raiser plays almost anything — seen it plenty" is appended mechanically to nearly every Vera/Priya line once triggered, even on folds where it adds nothing. The personas are differentiated (Mikko loose-aggro, Priya patient, Vera math-talk) and the leaky-recreational lines themselves are plausible, which lifts it off the floor, but the surface reads as scripted state-machines with flavor text, not people.

Only three opponents appear (Dunn, Mikko, Oyelaran) and each speaks from a small fixed template bank: the tag "The raiser plays almost anything — seen it plenty" is stamped verbatim on ~20 decisions regardless of context (even on Dunn's own fold when nobody re-raised light), Dunn always says "X is hopeless even for me," Mikko "nearly limped X out of boredom" five times word-for-word, and value lines like "a piece of this — betting for value" recur identically. Personas are distinguishable (Dunn the call-station, Oyelaran the odds-quoter, Mikko the loose aggressor) and pot-odds math adds flavor, but the zero variation in phrasing, no reaction to prior hands or moods, and slot-filled sentences read as a script with persona presets, not people.

Each player runs a tiny bank of slot-filled templates ("[hand] is hopeless even for me", "Nearly limped [hand] out of boredom. Nah", "Roughly N percent against M needed. Call") repeated verbatim across 30 hands, and the read tag "The raiser plays almost anything — seen it plenty" is stapled onto dozens of decisions, sometimes incoherently (appended to folds with no raiser context, or "re-raises light" after a simple open in hand 50). There are humanizing touches — distinct personas (Dunn the loose caller, Mikko the bored aggressor), tilt-flavored lines, occasional bad calls — but real recreational players never phrase the same thought identically twenty times or quote pot-odds percentages to the point. The variety is parameterized, not personal.
